To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Vps34 is required for p62 phosphorylation at Ser349, which is essential for the tumorigenesis of breast cancer cells, (2) the intact Vps34 structure is essential for its tumorigenic activity, and (3) Vps34-dependent p62 phosphorylation is mediated by PKC-δ.
Vps34, through the activation of p 62, is a novel oncogene that promotes tumor progression.
Vps34 promotes tumorigenesis by activating PKC-δ and p62.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of VPS34 in cancer cell growth.
the role of Vps33 in cancer cell proliferation and metastasis.
the role of Vps33 in the activation of PKC- δ- p62 for cancer progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Vps34 stimulation of pS349 of p62 for tumor progression.
Vps34, through its lipid kinase activity, transcriptional activity and protein-protein interactions, stimulates tumor development mainly by activating p62.
the Vps34/PKC-δ/p62 signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in cancer progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Vps34 promotes cancer progression through PKC- δ-mediated activation of p62.
Vps34 can be activated by caspase 2, which in turn activates PKC-δ, which in turn phosphorylates p62, which in turn increases the expression of Nrf2 and Vps34.
Vps34 promotes tumor development through the PKC-δ-dependent phosphorylation of p62.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Vps34, in the absence of caspase 1 and 11 cleavage, can be a novel target for cancer therapy.
Vps34 can activate p62 through a novel mechanism, which has not been reported before, and that this activation is essential for tumorigenesis.
Vps34, which is normally inactive in breast cancer cells, may be a potential therapeutic target to treat breast cancer.
